questions.question_text:
A $6$-pack of eggs costs $\$2.55$ and an $8$-pack costs $\$3.50$.
What is the cost per egg of the better buy? Answer to four decimal places.

options.why: This is the unit price of the $8$-pack, which is the dearer option per egg.
Averaged the two unit prices instead of choosing the lower one.
Divided $\$2.55$ by $8$, mixing the price of one offer with the size of the other.

questions.solution_text:
Option 1: $\dfrac{\$2.55}{6\text{ eggs}} = \dfrac{\$0.425}{1\text{ egg}}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{\$3.50}{8\text{ eggs}} = \dfrac{\$0.4375}{1\text{ egg}}$
$\$0.425 < \$0.4375$, so the better buy costs $\$0.4250$ per egg.

questions.question_text:
Sugar is sold in four different sized packets.
Which is the best buy?

options.why: Chose the largest packet, but $\$6.90 \div 2 = \$3.45$ per kg is dearer than $\$3.30$ per kg.
Chose the lowest total price, but $\$0.40$ for $100$ g is $\$4.00$ per kg — the dearest option.
Read the price straight off the $1$ kg packet without comparing the other packets per kilogram.

questions.solution_text:
$100$ g: $\dfrac{\$0.40}{0.1\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$4.00}{1\text{ kg}}$
$500$ g: $\dfrac{\$1.65}{0.5\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$3.30}{1\text{ kg}}$
$1$ kg: $\dfrac{\$3.50}{1\text{ kg}}$
$2$ kg: $\dfrac{\$6.90}{2\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$3.45}{1\text{ kg}}$
$\$3.30$ is the lowest, so $500$ g for $\$1.65$ is the best buy.

questions.question_text:
Coffee is sold in a $200$ g jar for $\$1.55$, a $0.5$ kg jar for $\$3.70$ and a $750$ g jar for $\$5.70$.
Which is the best buy?

options.why: At $\$7.60$ per kg this is cheaper than the $200$ g jar but dearer than the $0.5$ kg jar.
Chose the lowest total price; per kilogram it is the dearest at $\$7.75$.

options.text: The $0.5$ kg jar and the $750$ g jar are equally good value
options.why: Rounded both unit prices, $\$7.40$ and $\$7.60$ per kg, to the nearest $\$2$, giving $\$8$ per kg for both and hiding the difference.

questions.question_text:
Chips are sold in a $45$ g bag for $\$2.10$ and a $150$ g bag for $\$6.50$.
Comparing grams per dollar, which is the best buy? Round the rates to one decimal place.

options.text: The $150$ g bag, which gives $23.1$ g per $\$1$
The $45$ g bag, which gives $21.4$ g per $\$1$
options.why: Picked the smaller grams-per-dollar figure; with units per dollar the higher value is better.

options.text: The $150$ g bag, which gives $2.3$ g per $\$1$
options.why: Divided $150$ by $65$ instead of by $6.50$, shifting the answer by a factor of ten.

options.text: The $45$ g bag, which gives $94.5$ g per $\$1$
options.why: Multiplied $45$ by $2.10$ instead of dividing to get the amount per dollar.

questions.solution_text:
Option 1: $\dfrac{45\text{ g}}{\$2.10} \approx \dfrac{21.4\text{ g}}{\$1}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{150\text{ g}}{\$6.50} \approx \dfrac{23.1\text{ g}}{\$1}$
More grams per dollar is better value, so the $150$ g bag is the best buy.

questions.question_text:
Flour is sold in $2$ kg bags for $\$3.40$ and in $5$ kg bags for $\$8.25$.
What does $10$ kg of flour cost from each option, and which is the best buy?

options.why: Costed both correctly but then chose the dearer total for the same $10$ kg.
Multiplied the $2$ kg bag price by $2$ instead of by the $5$ bags that $10$ kg needs.
Multiplied each bag price by $10$ instead of by the number of bags needed for $10$ kg.

questions.solution_text:
Option 1: $10 \div 2 = 5$ bags
$5 \times \$3.40 = \$17.00$
Option 2: $10 \div 5 = 2$ bags
$2 \times \$8.25 = \$16.50$
For the same $10$ kg the $5$ kg bags cost less, so the $5$ kg bag is the best buy.

questions.question_text:
Iced tea is sold as $250$ mL for $\$2.00$, $600$ mL for $\$4.20$ and $1$ L for $\$7.50$.
Which bottle is the best buy?

options.why: Chose the lowest total price, but at $\$8.00$ per litre it is the dearest per unit.
Assumed the largest bottle must be best; at $\$7.50$ per litre it is beaten by the $600$ mL bottle.

options.text: The $250$ mL and $1$ L bottles are equally good value
options.why: Rounded the unit prices $\$8.00$ and $\$7.50$ per litre to whole dollars before comparing, giving $\$8$ per litre for both.

questions.solution_text:
$250$ mL: $\dfrac{\$2.00}{0.25\text{ L}} = \dfrac{\$8.00}{1\text{ L}}$
$600$ mL: $\dfrac{\$4.20}{0.6\text{ L}} = \dfrac{\$7.00}{1\text{ L}}$
$1$ L: $\dfrac{\$7.50}{1\text{ L}}$
$\$7.00$ is the lowest price per litre, so the $600$ mL bottle is the best buy.

questions.question_text:
A shop sells two $1.5$ L bottles of soft drink for $\$6.00$, or a pack of $10 \times 250$ mL cans for $\$5.50$.
Which is the best buy?

options.why: Calculated the rates correctly but chose the higher price per litre.
Divided $\$5.50$ by $10$ cans and treated the cost per can as the cost per litre.

options.text: The cans, because the bottles cost $\$4.00$ per litre
options.why: Divided the bottles' total price of $\$6.00$ by one bottle's $1.5$ L instead of the combined $3$ L.

questions.solution_text:
Bottles: $2 \times 1.5\text{ L} = 3\text{ L}$
$\dfrac{\$6.00}{3\text{ L}} = \dfrac{\$2.00}{1\text{ L}}$
Cans: $10 \times 250\text{ mL} = 2500\text{ mL} = 2.5\text{ L}$
$\dfrac{\$5.50}{2.5\text{ L}} = \dfrac{\$2.20}{1\text{ L}}$
$\$2.00 < \$2.20$, so the bottles are the best buy.

questions.question_text:
Which option gives the best value for money?
A: 250 ml for 32p; B: 500 ml for 60p; C: 1 litre for £1.10; D: 2 litres for £2.25.

options.why: Its unit price is 128p per litre, higher than the other options.
Its unit price is 120p per litre, which is more than option C.
Its unit price is 112.5p per litre, slightly higher than option C.

questions.solution_text: The unit prices are A: $32/0.25=128$ p/litre, B: $60/0.5=120$ p/litre, C: 110 p/litre, and D: $225/2=112.5$ p/litre. The smallest is option C.

questions.question_text:
Cereal is sold in a $600$ g box for $\$2.40$ and a $250$ g box for $\$1.10$.
Which is the best buy?

options.text: The $600$ g box, at $\$4.00$ per kg
The $250$ g box, at $\$4.40$ per kg
options.why: Calculated the rates correctly but chose the higher price per kilogram.

options.text: The $250$ g box, because it costs only $\$1.10$
options.why: Compared total prices instead of prices for the same quantity.

options.text: The $600$ g box, at $\$2.40$ per kg
options.why: Treated the $600$ g box as $1$ kg and used its total price as its price per kilogram.

questions.solution_text:
Option 1: $\dfrac{\$2.40}{600\text{ g}} = \dfrac{\$4.00}{1000\text{ g}}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{\$1.10}{250\text{ g}} = \dfrac{\$4.40}{1000\text{ g}}$
$\$4.00 < \$4.40$, so the $600$ g box is the best buy.

questions.question_text:
Bread rolls are sold in packs: A: $4$ for $\$0.52$; B: $6$ for $\$0.84$; C: $9$ for $\$1.08$; D: $12$ for $\$1.50$.
Compare the cost of exactly $36$ rolls from each option. Which is the best buy?

options.why: Chose the lowest pack price, but $9$ packs cost $\$4.68$, more than option C.
Chose a low pack price without comparing equal quantities; $6$ packs cost $\$5.04$, the highest total.
Assumed the largest pack must be best, but $3$ packs cost $\$4.50$, more than option C.

questions.solution_text:
A: $36 \div 4 = 9$ packs; $9 \times \$0.52 = \$4.68$
B: $36 \div 6 = 6$ packs; $6 \times \$0.84 = \$5.04$
C: $36 \div 9 = 4$ packs; $4 \times \$1.08 = \$4.32$
D: $36 \div 12 = 3$ packs; $3 \times \$1.50 = \$4.50$
For the same $36$ rolls, option C has the lowest cost and is the best buy.
